Glass vessels, shaped like two connected bulbs with a narrow passage between them, allowed sand to flow at a predictable rate. This invention flourished during the 13th century in Europe, where it became essential for navigation at sea and for daily timekeeping. The hourglass remained popular for centuries, serving as a practical tool before the development of accurate clocks and watches. Its elegant design and simplicity ensured its enduring appeal across cultures and generations.

rows.text: Volcanic islands form when tectonic activity creates underwater or surface volcanoes that accumulate lava and ash over time. These islands often emerge in chains along plate boundaries, particularly in the Pacific Ring of Fire, where they create dramatic landscapes with steep peaks and fertile soil. The volcanic activity that creates these islands can continue for millions of years, gradually building new land masses while occasionally causing destruction through eruptions. Despite their hazards, volcanic islands attract scientists and tourists alike due to their stunning natural beauty and unique ecosystems that develop on the nutrient-rich volcanic soil. rows.text: Harbor seals are marine mammals that live in coastal waters around the Northern Hemisphere. These spotted pinnipeds can dive to depths of over 600 feet and hold their breath for up to 30 minutes while hunting for fish and squid. They haul out on rocks and beaches to rest and reproduce and they often gather in large groups called haul-outs. Harbor seals have streamlined bodies with flippers that make them excellent swimmers and they communicate with each other through various vocalizations. These adaptable animals are found from California to the Arctic and they play an important role in their ocean ecosystems.
